what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 5 of 5: Long-range order under light-cone formation: close the gap in the doubled-graph argument. GIVEN (refereed): the light-cone formation law (record at (t+1,x) from (t,x) and (t,x +- e_j), weight exp(beta s.S)) is reversible with respect to pi(s) prop. to prod_x Z(beta|S_x(s)|); pi is the marginal on one layer of the nearest-neighbour Heisenberg ferromagnet on the doubled graph Gamma (two copies of Z^3, (x,0) joined to (y,1) for y in the 7-stencil of x); Gamma's Laplacian spectrum is {E, 14 - E}; pi is a range-2, many-body Gibbs law on Z^3 and block 19's pair reflection positivity does not transfer as is. THE GAP (referee): Gaussian domination on Gamma was proved only for layer-symmetric fields, because the reflections used preserve the bipartition (layer x spatial parity) and vertical edges never cross a reflection plane. Executed: |m| = 0.76 at beta = 1 on 24^3 and 48^3 planes (no decrease with size). TASK: prove long-range order of pi for the sphere menu at large beta. Routes: (i) find reflections of Gamma that do cross the layers (a reflection through a spatial site plane composed with the layer swap; check that the 7-stencil with its self-edge makes the vertical edges reflect onto themselves) and prove Gaussian domination for all fields, then the infrared bound with the {E, 14 - E} spectrum; (ii) show the layer-symmetric infrared bound already implies order of the one-layer marginal (the two layers are exchangeable under pi-bar); (iii) a Peierls-free route: a lower bound on E|S_x| via the sum rule, as in block 22's threshold argument (PR #8156). State the threshold beta you prove. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/lightcone-long-range-order/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/lightcone-long-range-order/<name>/check.py"
